We are looking for creative, motivated people interested in robotics, coding, electronics, and teamwork. Join us and turn ideas into reality!
summary:
MARSWALK is a browser-based Mars exploration console that takes users from the whole Solar System down to the surface of Jezero Crater. Users orbit a 3D Solar System, fly to Mars, then land at a base inspired by Perseverance’s site. There they drive a rover in 3D, complete ten field objectives and manage battery power. A tactical map offers elevation, slope and geology layers, hazard zones and an A* route planner that avoids steep slopes. A simulated environment feed, based on the kinds of readings Perseverance’s MEDA weather instruments take, lets users trigger dust storms and see how conditions change safe driving.

It addresses the challenge by turning NASA planetary data and mission concepts into something people can explore hands-on, with no installation. Planet constants, landing-site details and mission facts come from NASA sources. Terrain and weather are simulated models inspired by that data, not live telemetry.

It matters because planning human and robotic exploration depends on understanding terrain, hazards and resources. MARSWALK makes those ideas intuitive and engaging for students and the public, and it could later connect to real NASA elevation and telemetry data.
details:
MARSWALK is an interactive Mars exploration console that runs entirely in the browser, with nothing to install. It takes the user on one continuous journey: a 3D Solar System with procedural planets, moons and rings; a flight to Mars; and a landing at Jezero Crater, Perseverance’s landing site.

There the user gets two tools. A tactical map offers visible, elevation, slope and geology layers, and an A* route planner finds a safe path around steep slopes and hazard zones. It reports distance, drive time, climb, maximum slope and a Go, Caution or No-go verdict. A 3D rover game lets users drive between ten field objectives, manage battery and recharge at the habitat or solar farm, avoid hazards, and cope with dust storms. It has a minimap, three camera modes and touch controls.

It is meant to make mission-planning thinking about terrain, power and risk accessible to students and the public before any launch. Planet constants and mission facts come from NASA sources. The terrain is procedurally generated, and the weather feed (temperature, pressure, wind, dust, UV, radiation) is simulated and inspired by Perseverance’s MEDA instruments. Neither is real telemetry or real elevation data.

Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, THREE.js (GLSL shaders for the planets) and Leaflet for the map. We considered accessibility (no install, mobile support), scientific honesty (clearly separating real from simulated data), and playability.
